Getting started
Kansen helps you listen to and identify Hindustani swaras.
Students and listeners of classical music can benefit from learning to distinguish scales and the notes within them.
The app can complement your ear-training practice by playing notes for you to identify. This can help develop relative pitch: recognizing a note in relation to a reference note. Relative pitch can be learned and improved with practice, including in adulthood.
• All scales: explore and play notes.
• Training: practise identifying scales, swaras and octaves.
• Settings: Sound contains Instrument; Preferences contains Language and Theme; Help contains Manual.
• Use the back arrow to return.

Updates
In Settings, use Check for updates to look for a newer release. Checks run only when requested. Download the update, then tap Install and follow the Android prompt. APKs use temporary private storage, not Downloads; cached installers are removed after updating or when stale.

Language
Open Settings from the home page, then use Language to choose Marathi or English from the popup. Your choice is remembered.

Theme
Use Theme in Settings to choose Light, Dark or System. System follows your device theme and is the default. Your choice is remembered across app restarts.

Instrument
• Choose Harmonium or Pure tone in Settings. Harmonium is the default.
• Your choice is remembered across app restarts and applies to all notes, exercises and octave comparisons.
• Instrument sounds are synthesized from measurements of reference samples: their resonances, changes in tone and noise. The recordings themselves are not played. Pure tone has no added harmonics.
• All instruments use the same tuning. Harmonium and Pure tone fade in over 1 second and sustain while held.

Scales and keys
Choose from 12 scales: seven white and five black. The circle beside each scale indicates its tonic key colour.
• In the middle octave, White 1 starts at C4. The scales rise in semitone steps through B4.
• Select Lower, Middle or Upper octave from the dropdown. The lower octave is one octave below the middle; the upper octave is one octave above.
• On the Scales page, the harmonium has 12 swaras plus the next, higher Sa. The note identification keyboard has 12 swaras. Komal and tivra notes are labelled explicitly.
• Hold a key to hear it continuously; release it to stop. Its swara name and frequency in Hz appear below while held.
• Tap Sa beside the scale name to hear its reference Sa for 3 seconds.

Scale identification
A scale is selected at random.
• Refresh and Reveal stay disabled until you hold Play through the full 1-second fade-in. Releasing early does not count. Refreshing resets this requirement.
• Hold Play to hear its Sa continuously; release to stop. It stays the same until you refresh.
• Refresh: choose a different scale and hide the answer. Refresh and Reveal / Hide sit side by side below Play.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal the scale below the buttons.

Note identification
Choose a scale from the dropdown, or choose Random. The exercise uses the 12 swaras within one octave.
• Refresh and Reveal stay disabled until you hold both Play Sa and Play Swara through the full 1-second fade-in, separately. Releasing early does not count. Playing the keyboard keys does not unlock them. Refreshing or changing the scale resets this requirement.
• Hold Play Sa to hear the reference Sa, or hold Play Swara to hear the selected note. Release the button to stop.
• Play Sa highlights the Sa key while held. Play Swara does not highlight the target key, even if the target is Sa. Pressing a harmonium key directly highlights that key.
• Hold any of the 12 harmonium keys below Reveal / Hide to explore the current scale.
• Refresh: choose a different swara. With Random selected, the scale changes too. Refresh and Reveal / Hide sit side by side below the playback buttons.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal both the swara and its scale.
• The two buttons repeat the same pair until you refresh or change the dropdown selection. Changing the selection starts a new question.

Octave identification
• Choose a scale from the dropdown.
• Refresh and Reveal stay disabled until you hold Play through the full 1-second fade-in. Releasing early does not count. Refreshing or changing the scale resets this requirement.
• Hold Play to hear one random swara in a random octave within your chosen scale. Release to stop.
• Refresh: choose a new swara and random octave, keeping your selected scale. Refresh and Reveal / Hide sit side by side below Play. Play repeats the same note until you refresh or change the scale.
• Reveal / Hide: show or conceal the selected octave, scale and swara.
• After revealing, hold either of the two buttons below to hear the same swara in another octave. Release to stop. The selected scale and original question stay unchanged.
• The selected scale fixes the reference Sa in the middle octave: White 1 uses C4, rising through White 7 at B4. Identify the swara and octave relative to that reference.
• Scale and note identification exercises continue to use the middle octave.

Playback
• 1-second fade-in: Harmonium and Pure tone start silent and gradually reach full volume during their first second.
• The reference Sa button on the Scales page plays for 3 seconds, including the fade-in. Held notes fade in once and then sustain until you release.
• All training playback buttons have a play icon and sound while held, without a countdown or popup.
• Playback ends with a brief 20 ms fade-out to avoid a click.

Sound and tuning
• Use your device’s media volume to adjust loudness.
• The sounds are synthesized, not recordings of real instruments.
• Tuning uses 12-tone equal temperament with A4 = 440 Hz, like an equal-tempered harmonium. Raga-specific shruti adjustments are not modelled.
• Ear-training features work offline; checking for updates requires internet. Check your answers yourself: the exercises do not listen to or grade your singing.

Sound references
• Harmonium: Donya Quick. Reference excerpts prepared by Nicholaus P. Brosowsky / tonejs-instruments (CC BY 3.0): github.com/nbrosowsky/tonejs-instruments
• References were analyzed into spectral models and retuned for synthesis. No endorsement is implied. Licenses: creativecommons.org/licenses/by/3.0/
